name: Micro tasks

subjectOf.text: Because micro tasks require human judgment that machines cannot currently replace, they let organizations build products and outcomes that machines alone could not synthesize.
subjectOf.abstract: Because of the necessity of human judgment that cannot currently be replaced by machines/computers, micro tasks enable organizations to build products or create outcomes that cannot be synthesized by machines/computers alone.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: as of the current state of machine capability

subjectOf.text: Supervised machine learning currently depends on labelled data produced by micro task work, because unsupervised and reinforcement learning remain more complex and less relied upon for AI development.
subjectOf.abstract: While this may change as unsupervised and reinforcement learning evolve, currently, supervised learning depends on labelled data that is produced via micro task work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: current state of machine learning practice
may change as unsupervised and reinforcement learning evolve

subjectOf.text: The performance of an AI neural network's learning algorithm during supervised training rises with the quality and quantity of the labelled datasets it is trained on, which ties AI progress directly to micro task work.
subjectOf.abstract: The higher the quality and quantity of such labelled datasets the better the AI neural network's learning algorithm during the supervised training process.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Micro task platform systems carry significant limitations that hold back the evolution of AI itself, so platform design is a bottleneck on AI progress rather than a peripheral concern.
subjectOf.abstract: But alas, microtasks platform systems are subject to significant limitations that inhibit the evolution of AI.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Existing centralized micro task marketplaces cannot adequately meet the rising demand for high quality labelled AI training data.
subjectOf.abstract: The existing centralized marketplaces for micro task work cannot adequately fulfil the increasing demand for high quality micro task work for AI labelled training datasets.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: demand for high quality AI training datasets

subjectOf.text: Human shortcomings in micro task work such as limited attention span, irrationality, and inaccuracy create a need for verification, but manual verification fails as a remedy because the verifiers are subject to the same human limitations.
subjectOf.abstract: All too human shortcomings of micro task works, such as limited attention span, irrationality, and inaccuracies result in verification requirements for micro task work. However, manual verification of micro task work is subject to the same human limitations.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: manual verification of micro task work

subjectOf.text: To offset human limitations, requesters in centralized micro task structures assign the same task to teams of up to fifteen workers to form a consensus.
subjectOf.abstract: In an attempt to ensure quality of results and minimize the impact of the human limitations of their workers, requesters in centralized micro task structures set up teams of up to 15 workers to perform the same task in an effort to form a consensus.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Consensus by redundancy fails economically: multiplying the same work across many workers significantly increases the cost of micro task work.
subjectOf.abstract: The multiplication of work inherent in this process significantly increases the cost of micro task work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized platforms using redundant task assignment

subjectOf.text: Micro tasks are small tasks that require human judgment, can be completed by humans independently over the internet, and form part of a larger unified project.
subjectOf.abstract: Micro tasks are defined as small tasks that require human judgment, can be completed by humans independently over the internet, and are part of a larger unified project.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750

subjectOf.text: Supervised learning currently depends on labeled data produced by micro task work, so the evolution and growth of AI is correlated with the evolution and growth of micro task work.
subjectOf.abstract: currently, supervised learning depends on labeled data that is produced via micro task work
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750
scope_conditions: while supervised learning remains more common than unsupervised and reinforcement learning

subjectOf.text: Human limitations such as limited attention span, irrationality, and inaccuracy force verification of micro task work, but manual verification does not solve the problem because verifiers are subject to the same human limitations.
subjectOf.abstract: However, manual verification of micro task work is subject to the same human limitations.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750

subjectOf.text: Roughly 38 percent of the labor pool is unbanked but skilled and is therefore excluded from centralized micro task marketplaces, because without a bank account workers cannot contribute to or profit from those platforms.
subjectOf.abstract: the circa 38% of the labor pool that is unbanked but skilled does not currently have access to the centralized micro task marketplaces
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750

subjectOf.text: A reliable reputation score substitutes for redundant labor: if a high reputation worker completes a task, required duplication can fall from fifteen workers to five or fewer, which is what allows micro task work to scale.
subjectOf.abstract: If a reliable and high reputation score worker completes the tasks, the duplication may be brought from 15 to 5 or less in the decentralized CRDAO setup. This enables unprecedented scaling of micro task work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750
scope_conditions: decentralized platforms with portable, wallet linked reputation scores

subjectOf.text: Two sided reputation scores discipline both sides of the micro task market: workers become less likely to accept offers from low reputation requesters, and low reputation workers are less likely to be retained.
subjectOf.abstract: If requesters have a lower reputation score, workers become less likely to accept requesters
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750

subjectOf.text: Intermediary payment fees on centralized micro task platforms are economically viable only for high volume workers who can eventually avoid them, so those fees function as a barrier to entry for new micro task workers.
subjectOf.abstract: The fees in centralized mechanical turk platforms are only economically viable for higher volume workers who can at some point avoid the Paypal fees but create barriers to entry for new micro task workers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750

subjectOf.text: Reputation-weighted micro-task systems can potentially reduce human task redundancy from ten-to-fifteen-fold to five-fold or below through consistent, high-reputation agent outputs, accelerating production of superior datasets in sectors such as healthcare and finance.
subjectOf.abstract: By late 2025, such systems can potentially reduce human task redundancy from ten-to-fifteen-fold to five-fold or below through consistent, high-reputation agent outputs.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI's Mother's Instinct Engineered Consequence Emergent Ethics and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6244278
scope_conditions: based on comparative analysis of centralized versus reputation-weighted consensus systems
stated as a potential rather than realized reduction
